conceptual assets.information: The conditional coprocessor result is the rs1_i value when the recognized condition is true, or zero otherwise; the CPU depends on it as the result of the conditional instruction.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The result can contain operand data and is exposed through res_o at line 54, so an integration requiring confidentiality could observe it. The clocked logic assigns res_o from rs1_i or constants according to valid_cmd and condition at lines 53-57, so unauthorized modification can change the returned value. The valid_cmd and condition gates can withhold the rs1_i result and substitute zero at lines 53-57, losing the required operation result.
conceptual assets.attack: Observe res_o to obtain operand-derived data, or tamper with the result path or its control conditions so the instruction returns an incorrect or suppressed value.

conceptual assets.information: This is the predicate formed from the rs2_i zero comparison and the instruction condition bit that determines whether rs1_i is selected. It is an internal decision rather than a value carried directly through a port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The predicate can expose the zero or nonzero property of a potentially secret operand because res_o selection depends on it at lines 53-57. The predicate is produced by the comparison and condition logic at lines 62-63 and controls the result assignment at line 53, so altering it can select the wrong branch. The predicate can cause the rs1_i result to be withheld and replaced by zero through lines 53-57, blocking the intended transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: Observe the condition-dependent result to infer the comparison outcome, or fault the comparison path to force an incorrect or suppressed conditional result.

considered, not kept.reason: The opcode and function-field decode at lines 41-43 and its valid_o copy at line 66 only identify the supported operation, so the operation-selector rule bars them as a separate conceptual asset.
